title: Enterprise Onboarding: Support Process, Integration Checklist, Escalation Playbook, Health Checks & QBR
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Comprehensive enterprise onboarding playbook that unifies the support process, integration checklist, escalation matrix, known issues/workarounds, and the Health-check / QBR cadence for enterprise customers. Intended for CSMs, Support Engineers, SREs, and Customer Engineering.
content:
Overview:
This document provides a single-source reference for onboarding enterprise customers onto the Redwood Inference platform. It covers the support intake process, a step-by-step integration checklist, a formal escalation matrix with SLAs, regular health checks and QBR agendas, and a curated list of known issues with recommended workarounds. Use this playbook during the first 90 days of onboarding and maintain it as the customer moves into steady-state support.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-inference for enterprise customers to <= 5 business days.
- Provide clear SLA/resolution expectations and a deterministic escalation path.
- Ensure measurable operational health and an actionable QBR cadence.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Support Engineers
- Customer Engineering / Solutions Engineers
- Eng SRE & Oncall owners

1) Roles & responsibilities:
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): primary point of contact for commercial and adoption items. Coordinates QBRs and success plans.
- Support Engineer (Tier 2): owns technical triage, integration guidance, and reproducing customer issues.
- Oncall SRE (Tier 3): owns platform incidents impacting availability and P99 latency regressions.
- Customer Engineering (CE): assists with VPC, networking, and large-scale integration work.
- Head of Customer Success: final escalation for contractual or SLA disputes.

2) Support process (intake -> resolution):
1. Intake:
   - New enterprise customers open tickets via the Customer Portal or email enterprise-support@redwood.ai.
   - Tickets automatically tag by product area (generation, embeddings, private-deployments).
   - CSM performs initial triage within 8 business hours.
2. Triage:
   - Support Engineer acknowledges and sets severity within 1 business day.
   - Required triage artifacts: customer environment (hosted/dedicated/private), API keys (redacted), request IDs, sample payloads, timestamps, and relevant logs.
3. Diagnosis:
   - Reproduce on staging if possible. Attach request-id and example curl snippet.
   - If issue requires platform/infrastructure, escalate to Oncall SRE.
4. Resolution:
   - Share workaround or fix and document root cause in the ticket.
   - If bug, open internal engineering issue and link back to ticket.
5. Post-incident:
   - For P1/P2 incidents, produce a short incident summary and RCA within 3 business days.

Severity definitions & response targets:
- P1 (Service down / severe data loss): initial response 15 minutes (on-call), target remediation timeline communicated within 1 hour, RCA in 72 hours.
- P2 (Degraded critical functionality / large customer impact): initial response 1 hour, workaround within 8 hours, RCA in 5 business days.
- P3 (Minor impact / feature request): initial response 1 business day, fix scheduled as per roadmap.

3) Integration checklist (pre-launch):
- Account setup:
  - Confirm enterprise account and billing terms are finalized.
  - Create and rotate API keys; verify key has correct role scopes.
- Networking:
  - For Dedicated/Private: confirm VPC peering / private endpoint configuration. Provide sample Security Group rules: 
    | Protocol | Port | Source | Purpose |
    |---------:|:----:|:------:|:-------:|
    | TCP      | 443  | Customer CIDR | API traffic |
    | TCP      | 22   | Trusted IPs   | On-prem debug (if allowed) |
- IP allowlist: provide customer with our egress IP list and request their ingress allowlist.
- TLS & certs:
  - Verify TLS handshake to api.redwood.ai and custom endpoints for Private deployments.
- KMS & keys:
  - Confirm customer KMS integration (if enabled) and that encryption-at-rest keys are in place.
- Quotas & rate limits:
  - Agree on throughput targets and configure per-account rate limits. Example: 200 requests/sec sustained with 1,000 peak.
- Model selection & performance:
  - Recommend model variant and quantization profile for expected workload (see quantization-profiles page).
- Batching & retry policy:
  - Provide recommended batching window (e.g., 20ms) and retry/backoff policy (exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries).
- Observability:
  - Ensure customer has access to dedicated dashboards (latency, error-rate, token usage) and is granted read access to the QBR dashboard.
- Acceptance tests:
  - Run a smoke test suite that includes sample prompt generation, embeddings roundtrip, and rate-limit behavior.
  - Capture sample outputs to verify quality/regression baseline.

Example curl smoke-test snippet:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-v1.1", "input":"Hello world"}'

4) Escalation playbook (matrix & steps):
- Immediate escalation path for P1/P2 impacting production:
  1. Support Engineer (1st line) — try quick mitigations and provide runbook reference.
  2. Oncall SRE — if incident is platform-related (networking, GPU failures, database).
  3. Engineering owner (service-specific) — paging for code regressions or capacity saturation.
  4. CSM & Head of Customer Success — for contractual communication and customer updates.
- Communication protocol:
  - Post regular updates to the customer via the ticket and Slack channel (if provisioned) every 30 minutes for P1 until recovery.
  - Use the incident-status page for public outages; notify account team when a postmortem is published.
- Escalation contact list (example):
  - Support Engineer on-call: support-oncall@redwood.ai (rotating)
  - Oncall SRE pager: SRE PagerDuty (Escalation policy: 5m then 15m then manager)
  - Engineering owner alias: eng-service-owners@redwood.ai
  - Head of Customer Success: samantha.cho@redwood.ai

5) Health checks & QBR cadence:
- 30/60/90-day health checks during onboarding:
  - 30d: verify integration, smoke test pass, initial performance baseline.
  - 60d: usage ramp metrics, error rate < 0.5% sustained, P95 latency within expected target.
  - 90d: adoption metrics, run long-tail quality checks, schedule first QBR if usage > threshold.
- QBR recurring cadence (quarterly for enterprise):
  - Pre-QBR deliverables: usage and cost dashboard, recent incident summaries, model/regression report, feature requests backlog.
  - Sample QBR agenda:
    1. Executive summary (5m)
    2. Usage & adoption metrics (15m)
    3. Performance & reliability review (15m)
    4. Cost optimization opportunities (10m)
    5. Roadmap & feature asks (10m)
    6. Action items and owners (5m)
- Key metrics to track for QBRs:
  - Total API calls, tokens generated, embeddings volume
  - Error rate (5xx & 4xx split)
  - Latency P50/P95/P99 by route and model
  - Cost per 1k tokens and changes over time
  - Model quality regressions vs baseline prompt set

6) Known issues & workarounds (curated list):
- Issue: Intermittent 429s during bursts
  - Symptom: Short-lived increase in 429 responses under bursty traffic
  - Workaround: Implement client-side throttling with exponential backoff and jitter; request temporary burst increase from Capacity team.
  - Mitigation: Recommend burst queueing via batching to reduce token overhead.
- Issue: Longer tail P99 latency for long-context requests (> 8k tokens)
  - Symptom: P99 spikes above 1.5s for generation requests with >8k tokens
  - Workaround: Use a shorter context window for interactive requests; offload embeddings to asynchronous pipeline for background processing.
- Issue: Private deployment -- occasional TLS handshake failures when cert rotation overlaps
  - Symptom: Transient TLS errors for a small subset of clients during rotation windows
  - Workaround: Coordinate cert rotation windows in maintenance advisory; ensure dual-cert strategy for overlap.
- Issue: Embeddings drift / quality variance after model upgrade
  - Symptom: Embedding similarity scores changed vs baseline
  - Workaround: Pin an older model for critical production workflows and run a regression evaluation; schedule canary rollout for embedding models.

7) Post-onboarding handoff to steady-state support:
- Acceptance checklist complete and signed-off by CSM and customer.
- Transfer ownership: assign customer ticketing to Tier 2 queue; add customer dashboards to monitoring subscriptions.
- Schedule first quarterly QBR and recurring 30/60/90 reminders in calendar.

8) Templates & artifacts (links):
- Integration checklist template (copy into account page)
- Incident summary template (RCA)
- QBR slide template and metrics export scripts

9) Maintenance & periodic review:
- Owner: Customer Success Manager (CSM) must review this playbook with the account every 6 months.
- The document owner (Aisha Patel) will update platform-specific steps when the API or networking model changes.
